Subject: Data retention scope + rollback questions for EU tenancy

Hi Logan,

We're mapping out the final retention and deletion controls for our EU tenancy and have a couple of items we need Redwood to confirm before legal signs the SOW: 

- Canonical retention windows for daily backups vs. point-in-time snapshots (we expect to see both called out)
- Process for a customer-initiated rollback (is a full restore supported from backups / snapshots? SLA?)
- Whether Redwood can provide a temporary retention exception for backups/snapshots while we complete a migration (timeline request)
- Confirmation of subprocessors handling backups and whether any transfers leave the EEA (and DPA annex implications)

Can you send a short plan and a timeline (we're on a tight procurement schedule — aim to sign by 5/20). Attaching our procurement worksheet for context.

Thanks,
Jacob

Subject: Re: Data retention scope + rollback questions for EU tenancy

Hi Jacob — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kim and Naomi to pull the artifacts. High level response here and we'll follow up with a short deliverable: 

- Backups: account-level full backups are retained by default for 180 days in the EU region; encrypted at rest with customer-key option via our KMS integration.
- Snapshots: point-in-time snapshots are kept for 90 days by default. Snapshots can be used for customer-initiated rollback; restore SLA depends on dataset size — typical RTO for <1TB is 4-8 hours.
- Temporary exceptions: we can create a short-term retention exception (extension to 120/360 days depending on object type) for migration windows, subject to documented approval and an audit log entry.
- Subprocessors/transfers: list and geographies will be provided; cross-border movement only occurs for backups needed for disaster recovery and only to EU/UK/US regions as listed in the DPA.

We're preparing a concise "retention handoff + rollback plan" (PDF) and a CSV with snapshot exception examples. Expect the first package by tomorrow EOD (5/10). If you have a specific dataset or label that needs extended retention, please call that out.

Logan
Logan Wright
Head of Customer Engineering — Redwood Inference

Jacob — attaching the requested artifacts: retention_rollforward_plan.pdf and snapshots_exceptions.csv. Key excerpts below so you can triage quickly: 

- Default retention: backups = 180 days (encrypted), snapshots = 90 days.
- Rollback: supported from snapshots and from full backups. Snapshot restores are faster and recommended for small-scope rollbacks (RTO 4-8h). Full backup restores are supported for disaster recovery (RTO depends on dataset size; plan included).
- Deletion workflow: delete requests go through a 3-step orchestration: pre-delete validation -> soft-delete (30-day pending window for customer reversal) -> final purge. Soft-delete does not free capacity; purge is irreversible.
- Audit & evidence: each purge and retention-extension request is recorded and available via the Console audit logs. We can export logs for your auditors on request.
- Exceptions: For account-specific exceptions (e.g., migration hold), we can set snapshot retention to 120 days and extend backups to 360 days for a 90-day temporary window; exceptions require a signed DPA annex + internal SOC approval.

I'll follow up with the DPA redline separately (working with legal). If you need the subprocessor matrix now I can include the current list (we use two EU-based backup subproviders + a US DR provider; transfers to non-EEA are limited and justified for DR).

Attachments: retention_rollforward_plan.pdf; snapshots_exceptions.csv

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Ops — Redwood Inference
